rows.what_the_ink_shows: The final glyph in the primed display has a straight descending stem with a small closed bowl on its right and a separate prime: p′. The left-hand q′ of this same equality has a curved/open upper stroke and a different descending form. Thus the display visibly ends q′²=p′ (crops/51_scan011_L915_prime_equation.png). The nearby text naming p′ and q′ provides the same contrast between their upper strokes (crops/51_scan011_L915_letter_comparison.png). The lower, unprimed display does visibly end q²=q (crops/51_scan011_L915_unprimed_equation.png).
rows.note: Preserve q′²=p′ as written. The supplied intended idempotent relation is q′²=q′, consistent with the subsequent unprimed relation, but the final letter in the disputed display is a p with its bowl on the right. This is an authorial symbol slip rather than a transcription misreading; the equation was not silently corrected from mathematical expectation.

The right-side bowl supports p′, matching the original TeX. Retained the manuscript equation and recorded the supplied intended q′ relation without a proof check.
